**Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze - The candidate must be no more than 70 years old; as for education, when a person applies for a job, would they say, "I don't have a diploma, but I am educated"?! - The Synod must strictly follow the Statute of Management and Administration (28.04.2026, 11:40)**

"In the criteria, we read that [the candidate] must be Georgian, must be a monk, must be a member of the Synod, must have an education, and there is a reference to age, stating that they must have reached 40 years and be no more than 70 years old—this Synod does not have the right to change the Statute of Governance and must be strictly guided by the Statute of Governance," stated Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze, head of the Public Relations Department of the Patriarchate.
According to him, it is important for the life of the church that the established rule be observed.
"Today, three patriarchal candidates will be selected at the Synod, and the subsequent Synod, an expanded session, will be held to elect the Patriarch."

In the criteria, we read that [the candidate] must be Georgian, must be a monk, must be a member of the Synod, must have an education, and there is a specification regarding age: he must be at least 40 years old and no more than 70 years old.

I am a mathematician; the phrase "no more than 70 years" means that adding any amount of time to 70 means it is no longer "no more than 70." In other words, 70 plus some days and months is already more than 70. As a mathematician, this is crystal clear to me; however, let's see what decision the Synod will make regarding this.

The second point is that this Synod does not have the right to amend the Statutes of Governance and must strictly adhere to them. Regarding the issue of education, how can you imagine it: when a person does not have a diploma and applies for a job vacancy, what will they say—"I don't have a diploma, but I am an educated person"?! This won't work in any workplace.

Any issue can be subject to interpretation; for example, the question could be raised as to what it means to be Georgian. I had a friend who was Yezidi, but inwardly he was a very good Georgian; if we reason this way, everything can be called into question. There is also a concept of "hidden monks," and while the criterion here says "monk," a "hidden monk" means someone who has not been tonsured but lives a monastic life—meaning everything can be subject to interpretation. Therefore, I believe it is very important for the life of the Church that the established rules be upheld.
"We have already received information regarding the delegates from most of the dioceses," stated Andria Jaghmaidze.
